messages.subject: Re: rows full of NAs in detection history
parts:
Hi Gabriella,

It's unclear to me what you mean when you say you didn't detect one of the species at the station. In your y matrix for a given species, a value of 1 should represent that the species was detected at station i in occasion j, 0 means it was not detected at that station-occasion, and NA means you didn't sample during that station-occasion (which is different than not detecting the species). If you have NA for all occasions at a particular station you are telling occuMulti that you didn't sample at that station at all (or all the data was lost or something), and it therefore can't be used to help fit the model. This is true even if you have some non-missing values for other species at that station - if all occasions are NA at a station for any 1 species, you can't use that station.

Some unmarked functions drop a site with all missing values automatically but right now occuMulti does not. You would have to manually remove those stations (5,7..etc) from your dataset before you input them into your unmarkedFrame.

Ken

On Thursday, July 25, 2019 at 3:09:27 PM UTC-4, Gabriella Palomo wrote:
Hi everyone! 

I have a quick question. I am doing a co-occupancy model with occuMulti() between two species. I have stations (rows) where I didn't detect one of the species so it has NA across all columns (occasions). 

When I run the occuMulti() function I get the following error (those sites are the ones which have NAs across all occasions): 

Error in .local(umf, ...) : 
  No non-missing detections at sites: 5, 7, 10, 11, 13, 18, 22, 23, 24

What am I doing wrong?
